title: Defence Spending & Armed Forces Size
description: National defence investment as a percentage of GDP, military modernization, troop strength, and allied commitments.

officialFigureBenchmark.label: Current UK Defence Expenditure
officialFigureBenchmark.source: Ministry of Defence / NATO Defence Expenditure Report

publicOpinionQuestion: Do you support increasing UK defence spending to at least 2.5% of GDP?

labour.headline: Roadmap to 2.5% of GDP via Strategic Defence Review
labour.summary: Conducting a root-and-branch Strategic Defence Review (SDR) led by Lord Robertson to set out the pathway to 2.5% of GDP defence spending when economic conditions allow.
keyPoints: Unshakeable commitment to NATO and UK's continuous-at-sea nuclear deterrent (Trident)
Establish an Armed Forces Commissioner to champion service personnel welfare
Prioritize British-made military procurement and supply-chain resilience
Deepen European security pacts, including the 2024 UK-Germany Trinity House Defence Agreement
labour.costEstimate: Projected additional £6bn - £9bn per year when reaching 2.5%
labour.factCheckSnippet: Full Fact notes: The timing for reaching 2.5% remains contingent on the SDR and fiscal headroom.

conservative.headline: Legislate 2.5% of GDP on Defence by 2030 (Pathway to 3%)
conservative.summary: Officially committed to legislating defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030 (~£87bn/yr) with a sequenced pathway to 3.0%, ring-fencing the Dreadnought submarine programme and protecting the 73,000 regular Army personnel floor.
keyPoints: Target 2.5% of GDP by 2030 with a statutory timeline, scaling towards 3.0% as fiscal headroom expands
Protect regular British Army headcount with a strict 73,000 personnel floor
Ring-fenced sovereign capital funding for the Dreadnought nuclear submarine replacement
Deepen AUKUS and Global Combat Air Programme (Tempest) 6th-gen fighter alliances
conservative.factCheckSnippet: Full Fact / RUSI: Moving to 2.5% by 2030 requires ~£10bn/yr uplift above current baseline, funded by planned civil service reductions.

reform.headline: 3% GDP Defence Surge, 100k Regular Army, Veterans Dept & Navy Channel Patrols
reform.summary: Surge UK defence spending to 3% of GDP within 6 years, expand the regular British Army by 30,000 to 100,000 troops, establish a standalone Ministry for Veterans, grant tax exemptions for military pensions, and deploy the Royal Navy for Channel border interdiction.
keyPoints: 3% of GDP Defence Target & 100,000 Regular Army: recruit 30,000 additional regular troops with enhanced enlistment bonuses and fast-track recruitment
Standalone Department for Veterans: dedicated Cabinet-level Veterans Ministry guaranteeing priority access to housing, healthcare, and mental health support

Military Tax Relief & Sovereign Procurement: exempt active-duty overseas personnel and military pensions from basic-rate income tax; prioritise British defence factories and reject EU defence integration
Homeland Border Security Tasking: deploy Royal Navy vessels and maritime surveillance under Operation Restoring Justice to intercept unauthorized Channel crossings
reform.costEstimate: Estimated £20bn–£25bn/yr uplift at 3% GDP, funded via foreign aid cuts and Whitehall DOGE savings
reform.targetTimeline: 2.5% GDP by Year 3; 3.0% GDP within 6 years
reform.factCheckSnippet: RUSI / IFS: Expanding the regular Army from 73,000 to 100,000 reverses two decades of downsizing, though simultaneous £70bn+ tax cuts create significant fiscal tension.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK National Security & Veterans Contract

libdem.headline: Rebuild Conventional Army and Honour Armed Forces Covenant
libdem.summary: Reverse troop reductions, maintaining the Army at a minimum of 73,000, invest in European interoperability, and provide a legally binding Armed Forces Covenant.
keyPoints: Commit to 2.5% of GDP defence spending when public finances permit
Urgent recapitalization of military housing, veteran mental healthcare, and family support
Strengthen NATO joint air and maritime patrol in Baltic and High North
Strict parliamentary scrutiny before any foreign military deployments
libdem.costEstimate: Tied to economic recovery and standard NATO guidelines
libdem.factCheckSnippet: Independent Defence Review: Focuses strongly on personnel retention, but lacks specific funding formulas.

green.headline: Defensive Posture, Diplomacy & Scrap Trident Nuclear Weapons
green.summary: De-escalate international arms races, phase out the Trident nuclear deterrent, and redirect defence expenditure towards peacekeeping, cybersecurity, and climate resilience.
keyPoints: Cancel the Trident nuclear replacement programme and sign the UN Nuclear Ban Treaty
Retain defence spending at standard defensive levels focused on territorial protection
Halt arms exports to countries with documented human rights violations
Support service personnel with full trade union representation rights
green.costEstimate: Projected net saving of over £30bn over lifecycle by cancelling Trident
green.factCheckSnippet: House of Commons Library: Trident cancellation would reduce long-term capital liability, but involves costly decommissioning.

snp.headline: Removal of Trident from Scotland & Conventional Defence Force
snp.summary: Demand the immediate removal of nuclear weapons from HMNB Clyde (Faslane) and transition Scotland to a conventional Nordic-model defence force within NATO.
keyPoints: Ban nuclear weapons from Scottish sovereign soil and coastal waters
Retain Scottish maritime patrol vessels and shipbuilding contracts on the Clyde
Support NATO membership on conventional, non-nuclear terms (similar to Norway and Denmark)
Maintain total solidarity with Ukrainian self-defence against Russian aggression
snp.costEstimate: Proportionate share of conventional UK defence budget (~£3.5bn - £4bn for Scotland)
snp.factCheckSnippet: RUSI Analysis: Relocating Faslane nuclear facilities to an alternative UK base is estimated to take 10-15 years and £10bn+.

plaid.headline: Peace-First Defence, Veteran Care & Welsh Base Retention
plaid.summary: Oppose offensive foreign interventions, oppose nuclear renewal, and ensure fair defence infrastructure spending across Wales.
keyPoints: Oppose renewal of Trident nuclear weapons; invest savings in public health and education
Support Welsh defence industry workers while transitioning to civilian technologies
Full statutory support and guaranteed housing for all Welsh veterans
Oppose overseas combat missions without explicit UN mandate and parliamentary vote
plaid.factCheckSnippet: UK Parliament Research: Wales hosts key training establishments (e.g. RAF Valley, Brecon) requiring sustained maintenance.

restore.headline: Sovereign Re-Armament & Independent Homeland Defence
restore.summary: Rebuild British independent military power, expand naval fleet capacity, prioritize territorial defence, and end foreign nation-building missions.
keyPoints: Guaranteed 3% GDP floor for military expenditure to ensure true strategic autonomy
Substantially expand Royal Navy surface fleet and attack submarines built in UK yards
Restore National Service options in engineering, cyber, and military reserves
Abolish diversity and political training in the Armed Forces to focus purely on combat readiness
restore.costEstimate: Requires £20bn+ annually financed via quango abolition and foreign aid reprioritization
restore.factCheckSnippet: IFS / OBR: Eliminating overseas aid and quangos yields under £12bn, which does not cover a sustained 3% GDP expansion.

title: Taxation, National Debt & Fiscal Policy
description: Tax thresholds, wealth taxation, National Insurance, business rates, and government borrowing rules.
publicOpinionQuestion: Do you support increasing taxes on high earners and wealth to fund public services?

labour.headline: Chancellor Healey's Fiscal Rules & Pension Tax Safeguard
labour.summary: Led by Chancellor John Healey, maintaining strict fiscal rules on day-to-day spending while guaranteeing low-income pensioners are protected from income tax drag during this Parliament.
keyPoints: Guarantee that low-income pensioners relying on the basic state pension will not be dragged into paying income tax in this Parliament
Balanced day-to-day budget funded strictly from tax receipts, with borrowing focused on productive capital projects
Safeguarded funding commitments for the NHS and foundations of the new National Care Service
Targeted wealth and capital contribution reviews alongside crackdowns on corporate tax loopholes
labour.costEstimate: Maintains day-to-day budget surplus while ring-fencing social care investments
labour.factCheckSnippet: OBR confirmed: Safeguarding low-income pensioners from the personal allowance freeze provides targeted relief for state-dependent retirees.

conservative.headline: Tax Cuts, Civil Service Rollback & Enterprise Deregulation
conservative.summary: Reverse tax burdens on businesses, cut administrative state costs, scrap the employer NI increase, and cut public spending waste.
keyPoints: Reverse the increase in Employer National Insurance
Abolish inheritance tax for family homes and family-owned farms
Maintain freeze on corporation tax rate and expand full expensing for capital equipment
Cap welfare spending and force work-capable claimants into employment
conservative.factCheckSnippet: IFS notes: Welfare savings of this magnitude historically face significant legal and delivery obstacles.

reform.headline: £20k Tax Threshold, 'Britannia Card' (£250k Non-Dom Dividend), UK DOGE & 15% Corp Tax
reform.summary: Overhaul the tax and state system led by Nigel Farage, Richard Tice, and Robert Jenrick: raise the income tax starting threshold toward £20,000, launch the £250,000 'Britannia Card' non-dom wealth visa to fund a direct tax-free dividend for low-paid British workers, deploy Zia Yusuf’s UK 'DOGE' efficiency units, cut Corporation Tax to 15%, and rescue pubs/hospitality.
keyPoints: Lift Personal Tax Allowance toward £20,000 & Abolish IR35: free up to 7 million low earners from income tax, scrap IR35 rules for sole traders/contractors, and abolish inheritance tax on estates under £2m

The 'Britannia Card' (£250k Non-Dom Wealth Visa): 10-year residency permit for wealthy global investors with 100% of fee revenue distributed directly as a tax-free 'Robin Hood' annual bonus to the bottom 10% of full-time UK workers
UK 'DOGE' (Department of Government Efficiency): deploy forensic auditors and AI data teams across local councils and Whitehall to cancel consultancy contracts, scrap DEI roles, and slash state waste
15% Corporation Tax & Pubs/Hospitality Package: cut Corporation Tax from 25% to 15%, slash beer duty by 10p a pint, cut small business employer NI, and reform punitive high-street business rates
reform.costEstimate: Claims £50bn+/yr savings from DOGE, Net Zero repeal, and Bank of England QE interest reform; IFS estimates £70bn+ net tax cut cost
reform.targetTimeline: Immediate Year 1 Emergency Budget & DOGE deployment
reform.factCheckSnippet: IFS Analysis: The £250k Britannia Card could attract wealthy non-doms but risks reducing standard HMRC tax yields from existing UK-resident high earners.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK Economic Growth, Britannia Card & DOGE Blueprint

libdem.headline: Windfall Taxes on Banks & Tech Giants for Public Services
libdem.summary: Restore fairness by raising taxes on big banks, energy super-profits, and tech monopolies, while reversing stealth income tax threshold freezes.
keyPoints: Raise the Bank Surcharge and Bank Levy to pre-2016 levels
Introduce a permanent windfall tax on fossil fuel company super-profits
Digital Services Tax quadrupled on social media and global tech giants
Reform capital gains tax so investment income is taxed on par with labor income
libdem.factCheckSnippet: IFS: Policy targets high earners and profitable corporations with clear costing, though bank tax changes risk financial city flight.

green.headline: Annual Wealth Tax on Multi-Millionaires & Carbon Tax
green.summary: Introduce a 1% annual wealth tax on assets over £10m and 2% over £1bn, equalise capital gains with income tax, and institute a carbon border tax.
keyPoints: 1% annual tax on individual net wealth above £10m; 2% on wealth above £1bn
Abolish the upper earnings limit on National Insurance so high earners pay full rate
Introduce a comprehensive carbon tax starting at £120/tonne
Massive £40bn annual green transformation public investment
green.factCheckSnippet: Tax Policy Associates / IFS: Wealth taxes yield revenue but risk capital flight and valuation administrative friction.

snp.headline: Progressive Taxation & UK-Wide Austerity Reversal
snp.summary: Defend Scotland's progressive income tax tiers (higher rates for top 10%), push Westminster to end austerity and abolish the two-child benefit limit.
keyPoints: Maintain progressive Scottish tax bands where top earners contribute more
Demand UK devolution of all tax powers including National Insurance and VAT
Scrap the two-child benefit limit immediately (lifting 250,000 children from poverty)
Reinvest oil and gas tax receipts into a national Scottish Sovereign Wealth Fund
snp.costEstimate: Scottish tax changes generate ~£1.5bn in devolved revenue
snp.factCheckSnippet: Scottish Fiscal Commission: Scottish progressive tax system generates positive net revenue with modest behavioural drag.

plaid.headline: Fair Funding Formula for Wales & Wealth Redistribution
plaid.summary: Replace the Barnett formula with a needs-based funding settlement for Wales, worth an additional £1.2bn annually, and support UK-wide wealth taxes.
keyPoints: Abolish the Barnett Formula; install an independent funding formula matching Welsh demographic need
Reclaim £4bn in rail consequentials owed from the HS2 project
Support UK-wide equalisation of capital gains tax with income tax
Devolution of Crown Estate land and natural resources to Wales
plaid.costEstimate: Targeted £1.2bn annual budget enhancement for Wales
plaid.factCheckSnippet: Holtham Commission & Welsh Governance Centre: Barnett formula consistently produces per-capita underfunding relative to Welsh health need.

restore.headline: Flat Tax Framework & Dismantling Government Waste
restore.summary: Dramatically lower marginal tax rates, replace complex tax loopholes with a streamlined flat tax rate, and cut government spending by 25%.
keyPoints: Transition towards a simple 20% flat tax on earnings and business profits
Immediate abolition of all Stamp Duty and Inheritance Tax
Abolish 50+ regulatory quangos and halve central government department expenditure
Repatriate corporate profits with zero tax on domestic manufacturing reinvestment
restore.costEstimate: Demands over £100bn in public spending contraction
restore.factCheckSnippet: Economic Consensus: Flat tax schemes of this scale historically lead to severe short-term revenue contractions and borrowing spikes.

title: NHS Waiting Lists, Staffing & Social Care
description: Strategies to eliminate the 7M+ patient backlog, address ambulance delays, recruit clinicians, and reform social care.
publicOpinionQuestion: Is the NHS heading in the wrong direction and in urgent need of major structural reform?

labour.headline: Founding the National Care Service & NHS Community Shift
labour.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham's flagship commitment to establish a universal National Care Service, funded long-term by transitioning pensions to a double lock from 2030, alongside urgent NHS waiting list reductions.
keyPoints: Establish a National Care Service with national standards and fair pay agreements for care workers
Retain the pensions triple lock for this Parliament, transitioning to a double lock in April 2030 to sustainably fund social care
Ensure low-income pensioners on the basic state pension are not dragged into paying income tax in this Parliament
Deliver 40,000 extra elective appointments and scans each week while shifting care from hospitals to community hubs
labour.costEstimate: Funded by tax compliance and long-term 2030 double-lock pension reform savings
labour.targetTimeline: Phased implementation with full Care Service framework by 2030
labour.factCheckSnippet: Conference verified: The government committed to keeping the triple lock through this Parliament before shifting to a double lock in April 2030.

conservative.headline: NHS Long-Term Workforce Plan & 40 New Hospitals Programme
conservative.summary: Deliver the Long-Term Workforce Plan to double medical school places, construct community diagnostic centres, and expand Pharmacy First.
keyPoints: Expand Pharmacy First to free up 10 million GP appointments
Double medical school places to 15,000 a year and nurse training places
Build 100 new community diagnostic hubs across regional shopping centers
Cap social care lifetime costs at £86,000 (though delayed until 2025/26)
conservative.costEstimate: Funded within existing 2.4% baseline NHS real-terms settlement
conservative.factCheckSnippet: National Audit Office (NAO): The 40 new hospitals programme suffered major delays, inflation overruns, and required redesign.

reform.headline: European-Style Insurance Funding Reform, 31-Day Voucher Right & Frontline Tax Breaks
reform.summary: Keep healthcare free at the point of delivery while transitioning away from the centralised Whitehall NHS funding model toward a European-style social health insurance and voucher system, giving patients waiting over 31 days an automatic private treatment voucher and granting 20% tax relief on private healthcare.
keyPoints: Reform Centralised NHS Funding Model: transition toward a French/German-style insurance and independent provider model while keeping treatment free at the point of delivery
31-Day Waiting List Voucher Guarantee: automatic legal right to an NHS-funded private healthcare voucher if waiting more than 31 days for a GP or consultant appointment/operation
20% Private Healthcare Tax Relief: grant 20% tax relief on all private medical insurance and self-funded surgery to encourage millions who can afford it to relieve pressure on NHS beds
Zero Basic-Rate Tax for Frontline Staff & Cut Bureaucracy: exempt frontline NHS doctors and nurses from basic-rate income tax for 3 years and eliminate all DEI and non-clinical management bloat
reform.costEstimate: Estimated £17bn/yr for vouchers, tax breaks, and insurance relief
reform.factCheckSnippet: Nuffield Trust / King’s Fund: While European social health insurance systems achieve shorter waits, they typically spend a higher share of GDP on healthcare than the UK.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK Healthcare & Waiting List Reform Plan

libdem.headline: Legal Right to See a GP in 7 Days & Free Personal Care
libdem.summary: Introduce a legal right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours in urgent cases), provide 8,000 more GPs, and implement free personal social care.
keyPoints: Hire 8,000 more permanent full-time GPs funded by digital service taxes
Introduce free personal care for elderly and disabled adults (Scottish model)
Establish a dedicated 24/7 mental health emergency helpline and local walk-ins
National Carer's Minimum Wage set £2 above the standard minimum wage
libdem.costEstimate: Costed at £8.4bn per year funded by tax on banks and tech firms
libdem.factCheckSnippet: King's Fund: Free personal care is widely regarded as transformative for freeing hospital discharge beds, though recruitment bottlenecks persist.

green.headline: £50bn Health & Social Care Investment & End All Privatisation
green.summary: Increase NHS funding by £30bn per year and social care by £20bn, bring all outsourced services back in-house, and provide immediate pay restoration for junior doctors.
keyPoints: Inject £50bn annually funded by progressive wealth and carbon taxation
Repeal all legislation introducing private competition in the NHS
Full pay restoration for doctors, nurses, and allied healthcare professionals
Comprehensive free NHS dentistry for every UK resident
green.factCheckSnippet: Health Foundation: Would fully solve NHS capital depreciation and staffing deficits, but relies on unprecedented wealth tax collection.

snp.headline: Protect NHS Scotland & Enact 'Keep the NHS Public' Law
snp.summary: Protect Scotland's highest per-capita health spending in the UK, demand a UK-wide 'Keep the NHS in Public Hands' Act, and boost Scottish social care pay.
keyPoints: Legislate to prevent future UK trade deals opening NHS procurement to US corporations
Maintain Scotland's free prescriptions and free personal care for over 65s
Increase minimum pay for Scottish adult care workers to £12.50+ an hour
Demand £1.6bn Barnett consequential uplift from UK health spending
snp.factCheckSnippet: Audit Scotland: NHS Scotland per capita spending is 7% higher than England, but waiting time pressures remain acute across acute trusts.

plaid.headline: Welsh Health Rescue Plan & Rural Dental Services
plaid.summary: Overhaul Welsh NHS management, restore dental services across rural Wales, recruit Welsh-speaking healthcare workers, and retain medical graduates.
keyPoints: Full student debt forgiveness for medical and nursing graduates who work in Wales for 5 years
Establish an independent Welsh Medical Inspectorate to eliminate regional waiting disparities
Universal access to NHS dental registrations in every local authority
Urgent reform of Welsh ambulance service discharge and handovers
plaid.costEstimate: Funded through restructured Welsh devolved budget allocation
plaid.factCheckSnippet: Welsh NHS Confederation: Debt-forgiveness schemes prove effective for regional clinician retention in rural Welsh communities.

restore.headline: Decentralise NHS into Local Mutuals & Cut Non-Clinical Diversity Units
restore.summary: Break up the monolithic NHS central bureaucracy into locally governed mutual trusts, eliminate all non-clinical administrative overhead, and prioritize front-line clinical care.
keyPoints: Transfer hospital ownership to local doctor-and-patient mutual co-operatives
Immediate dismissal of all diversity, inclusion, and political officers across all trusts
Prioritize British citizens for non-emergency medical treatment over medical tourism
Incentivise domestic medical training while reducing reliance on foreign staff poaching
restore.costEstimate: Aims to save £5bn in administrative overhead to redirect into frontline beds
restore.factCheckSnippet: Kings Fund / NHS England: Non-clinical diversity roles account for less than 0.1% of the NHS £180bn budget.

compass.summary: Publicly funded universal healthcare & social care

title: Immigration, Border Security & Asylum
description: Net migration levels, work and student visa salary thresholds, Channel small boats, and asylum processing.

officialFigureBenchmark.label: UK Net Migration & Asylum Backlog (2025/26)
officialFigureBenchmark.value: Net migration falling from 685k peak; Earned Settlement (10-yr ILR) & ECHR debates active
officialFigureBenchmark.source: Office for National Statistics (ONS) / Home Office

publicOpinionQuestion: Should immigration into the UK be significantly reduced over the next 5 years?

labour.headline: Earned Settlement (10-Yr ILR), IIAA Fast-Track Appeals & Border Command
labour.summary: Enacting the 'Restoring Order and Control' White Paper and Immigration & Asylum Bill: replacing automatic 5-year settlement with a 10-to-15-year 'Earned Settlement' (ILR) route, replacing first-tier tribunals with the Independent Immigration Appeals Authority (IIAA), tightening ECHR Article 8 claims, and smashing smuggler gangs via the Border Security Command.
keyPoints: Earned Settlement Overhaul: extend Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) qualifying timelines from 5 to 10+ years based on economic contribution and B2 English proficiency
Independent Immigration Appeals Authority (IIAA): fast-track adjudicators to clear asylum backlogs and curb ECHR Article 8 (family life) and Modern Slavery loopholes
'Core Protection' Asylum Model: shift to temporary 30-month reviewable protection periods and require asylum seekers with assets to contribute toward accommodation costs
Border Security Command & Skills Linkage: counter-terror powers against smuggling gangs while barring overseas care worker recruitment without domestic workforce training plans
labour.costEstimate: £150m+ Border Security Command & IIAA setup; saves £1bn+/yr closing asylum hotels
labour.targetTimeline: Immigration and Asylum Bill & White Paper rules active across 2025–2027
labour.factCheckSnippet: Migration Observatory: Extending ILR from 5 to 10 years significantly increases total visa fee and Immigration Health Surcharge revenues while reducing permanent settlement rates.
labour.officialSourceTitle: Restoring Order and Control: Home Office White Paper & Bill

conservative.headline: Leave the ECHR, US-Style 'Removals Force' (150k/yr) & Binding Cap
conservative.summary: Following Lord Wolfson's legal review, Kemi Badenoch formally committed the Conservative Party to leaving the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), repealing the Human Rights Act, establishing a dedicated 'Removals Force' targeting 150,000 deportations a year, and imposing a legally binding annual cap on net migration.
keyPoints: Formal Manifesto Pledge to Leave the ECHR & Repeal the Human Rights Act to eliminate judicial blocks on deportations
Dedicated 'Removals Force' (150,000/yr Target): US ICE-style enforcement agency to detain and deport illegal entrants and foreign national offenders
Abolish Immigration Tribunals & Legal Aid: scrap judicial reviews, standard tribunal appeals, and legal aid for unauthorized border crossings
Binding Annual Parliament Cap & Restricted ILR: strict parliamentary cap on work/family visas and bar temporary visa holders from automatic permanent settlement or welfare
conservative.costEstimate: Funded by cutting asylum legal aid and hotel accommodation contracts
conservative.targetTimeline: Immediate ECHR withdrawal bill in Year 1
conservative.factCheckSnippet: Institute for Government / Wolfson Review: Leaving the ECHR removes Strasbourg injunctions but requires renegotiating parts of the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement and Good Friday frameworks.
conservative.officialSourceTitle: Conservative Borders Plan & Wolfson ECHR Commission

reform.headline: 5-Yr Asylum Freeze (Void 90k Claims), 1M+ Deportations, Abolish ILR & Visa Sanctions
reform.summary: Comprehensive border and residency overhaul unveiled by Nigel Farage and Zia Yusuf: completely suspend the UK asylum system for 5 years, void ~90,000 pending asylum claims, target 'north of 1 million' deportations via a UK Deportation Command, abolish Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), bar foreign nationals from welfare/social housing, and impose visa bans, asset freezes, flight bans, and tariffs on countries refusing deportees.
keyPoints: 5-Year Asylum Suspension & Voiding 90,000 Pending Claims: enact the Illegal Migration (Mass Deportation) Bill to suspend all asylum claims for 5 years, void ~90,000 pending applications, abolish asylum tribunals, and review post-2024 grants

Deport 'North of 1 Million People' & UK Deportation Command: establish a dedicated Deportation Command under 'Operation Restoring Justice' utilizing detention capacity, third-country agreements, and direct return deals (including Afghanistan and Eritrea)

Visa Bans, Asset Freezes, Flight Bans & Tariffs on Uncooperative States: penalize countries refusing deported nationals (naming Pakistan, Afghanistan, Syria, Eritrea, Sudan, Somalia) with immediate visa suspensions, London asset freezes, airspace bans, and trade tariffs

Abolish Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) & Public Funds Ban: scrap permanent settlement (ILR) in favour of 5-year renewable work visas at £45k–£60k+ salary thresholds, extend citizenship timelines, and restrict all welfare and social housing strictly to British citizens
Leave the ECHR & Repeal the Human Rights Act: withdraw from the European Convention on Human Rights and disapply the 1951 Refugee Convention to end judicial blocks on removals
reform.costEstimate: Claims £10bn+/yr savings by ending asylum hotels, foreign national welfare, and legal aid
reform.targetTimeline: Immediate Day-1 emergency legislation & 5-year parliamentary term freeze
reform.factCheckSnippet: Oxford Migration Observatory / IFS: Retrospectively scrapping ILR and deporting 1m+ people faces major diplomatic, logistical, and sector workforce hurdles in health and hospitality.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK: Operation Restoring Justice, Hythe Visa Sanctions & ILR Abolition

libdem.headline: Fair & Humane Asylum System & Restore Dependants for Carers
libdem.summary: Transfer asylum decision-making from the Home Office to a new independent agency to clear backlogs, allow asylum seekers to work after 3 months, and fix care worker shortages.
keyPoints: Create a dedicated, independent asylum processing agency to decide claims within 3 months
Grant asylum seekers the right to work if their claim has been pending for over 3 months
Repeal the Illegal Migration Act and create safe and legal humanitarian routes
Exempt vital care workers from restrictive dependant bans to prevent care home closures
libdem.costEstimate: Saves £4bn by closing emergency asylum hotels within 12 months
libdem.factCheckSnippet: Refugee Council / Home Office data: Allowing asylum seekers to work generates an estimated £300m in tax revenues and reduces state hotel dependency.

green.headline: Abolish Hostile Environment, Safe Routes & Climate Visas
green.summary: Dismantle the 'Hostile Environment', create safe and legal routes for refugees, grant all asylum seekers the right to work, and introduce humanitarian visas for climate refugees.
keyPoints: End all immigration detention centres and replace them with community-based support
Full right to work for asylum seekers from the day they arrive
Abolish the minimum income requirement for British citizens bringing foreign spouses (£29,000 threshold)
Lead global treaty on humanitarian protections for climate-displaced populations
green.costEstimate: Funded through redirection of immigration enforcement and detention budgets
green.factCheckSnippet: Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants: Removing spouse income rules reunites thousands of British families, but would increase net migration numbers.

snp.headline: Scottish Visa Scheme & Devolved Migration Powers
snp.summary: Demand full devolution of immigration powers to introduce a Scottish Visa tailored to Scotland's acute rural depopulation and workforce aging challenges.
keyPoints: Create a Scottish Rural Visa Pilot to attract doctors, care workers, and engineers
Lower arbitrary UK salary thresholds that harm Scottish businesses and hospitality
End the hostile environment and close Dungavel Immigration Removal Centre
Re-establish free movement with the EU following Scottish independence
snp.costEstimate: Funded within Scottish economic development allocations
snp.factCheckSnippet: National Records of Scotland: Scotland is the only UK nation where all projected population growth relies on inward net migration.

plaid.headline: Wales as a Nation of Sanctuary & Devolved Work Visas
plaid.summary: Establish Wales as an official Nation of Sanctuary, decentralise visa rules to address Welsh farming and NHS shortages, and provide comprehensive language integration.
keyPoints: Devolve immigration quota powers to the Senedd to fill critical gaps in Welsh agriculture and social care
Immediate closure of inappropriate emergency asylum accommodation sites in Wales
Provide free Welsh and English language courses for all arriving refugees
Campaign for humane, safe, and legal asylum routes across the UK
plaid.factCheckSnippet: Welsh Refugee Council: Regional visa schemes exist successfully in Canada and Australia, providing tested international precedents.

restore.headline: Complete Border Lockdown & Sovereign Repatriation
restore.summary: Seal UK territorial borders, deploy the Royal Navy to turn back illegal craft, enforce strict zero-net-migration, and conduct audits of illegal visa overstayers.
keyPoints: Deploy the military and maritime forces to interdict and intercept all unauthorised vessels
Immediate repatriation of all illegal entrants without legal appeals
Moratorium on low-skilled foreign labor permits across all sectors
Mandatory biometric national identity card system to prevent illegal employment
restore.costEstimate: Financed by immediate elimination of £4bn+ asylum accommodation contracts
restore.factCheckSnippet: Maritime Law Experts: Forcible maritime pushbacks in the Channel violate the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and require French territorial cooperation.

title: Energy Security, Net Zero & North Sea Oil
description: 2030 clean power targets, Great British Energy, North Sea oil and gas extraction, and heat pump mandates.

officialFigureBenchmark.label: UK Renewable Electricity Share
officialFigureBenchmark.source: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)

publicOpinionQuestion: Do you support the UK's legal target of reaching Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050?

labour.headline: Great British Energy & Clean Power by 2030
labour.summary: Set up publicly owned Great British Energy with £8.3bn capital; double onshore wind, triple solar power, and quadruple offshore wind by 2030; end new North Sea drilling licenses.
keyPoints: Capitalise Great British Energy headquartered in Aberdeen with £8.3bn
No new exploration licenses issued for North Sea oil and gas
Lift the de facto planning ban on onshore wind farms in England
Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to insulate 5 million homes and cut household energy bills
labour.costEstimate: £8.3bn for GB Energy + £6.6bn for Warm Homes over parliament
labour.factCheckSnippet: National Grid ESO: Clean power by 2030 is technically possible but requires unprecedented speed in grid infrastructure connections.

conservative.headline: Pragmatic Net Zero, North Sea Licences & SMR Nuclear
conservative.summary: Maintain the 2050 Net Zero target while preventing punitive consumer costs; mandate annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds; fast-track Small Modular Nuclear Reactors (SMRs).
keyPoints: Annual statutory licensing rounds for domestic North Sea oil and gas production
Scrap boiler phase-out fines and delay electric vehicle sales mandates to 2035
Invest £1bn in Small Modular Nuclear Reactor development and nuclear fusion research
Protect consumers from sudden green levies added onto domestic electricity bills
conservative.costEstimate: Market-led capital expenditure with selective government loan guarantees
conservative.targetTimeline: 2050 Net Zero target with relaxed milestones
conservative.factCheckSnippet: Climate Change Committee (CCC): Watering down interim deadlines makes achieving the legally binding 2050 target significantly harder.

reform.headline: Scrap Net Zero, Nationalise British Steel & 50% Public Ownership of Water Utilities
reform.summary: Abandon Net Zero entirely and repeal the Climate Change Act to slash industrial and household energy bills, fast-track North Sea oil, gas, and shale fracking, while adopting strategic industrial intervention by nationalising British Steel (#SaveOurSteel) and taking failing water utilities into 50% public ownership.
keyPoints: Repeal Net Zero & Climate Change Act: scrap all Net Zero targets, green levies, heat pump mandates, and EV sales bans to cut energy bills and re-industrialise Britain
Nationalise British Steel (#SaveOurSteel): bring primary British steelmaking and blast furnaces into sovereign public ownership to protect national security and working-class industrial jobs
50% Public Ownership of Water Companies: restructure indebted water utilities into a 50% state-owned, 50% British pension-fund-owned model with strict sewage enforcement
Fast-Track North Sea Oil, Gas & British SMRs: mandate immediate North Sea oil and gas licensing, lift bans on domestic shale gas fracking, and build UK-designed Small Modular Nuclear Reactors
reform.costEstimate: Claims £30bn/yr saved from green subsidies; steel/water stakes financed via debt restructuring
reform.targetTimeline: Immediate statutory repeal of Net Zero in Year 1
reform.factCheckSnippet: Full Fact / Ofgem: Cutting green levies saves ~£150–£170/yr on average household bills, while partial water nationalisation requires complex bondholder restructuring.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK Energy Independence, #SaveOurSteel & Utility Ownership Plan

libdem.headline: 80% Renewable Electricity by 2030 & Ban Dirty Water Dumping
libdem.summary: Drive 80% renewable electricity by 2030, launch an Emergency Home Energy Upgrade programme, hold water company bosses criminally accountable for sewage, and restore solar incentives.
keyPoints: Cut VAT on domestic solar panels, battery storage, and heat pump installations to zero
Emergency insulation drive focused on low-income and fuel-poor households
Re-introduce the 2030 ban on new petrol and diesel cars
Transform water companies into public benefit corporations with strict environmental fines
libdem.costEstimate: £10bn over 5 years financed by permanent windfall taxes on fossil fuels
libdem.factCheckSnippet: Energy UK: Zero VAT and grant subsidies have proven high uptake for heat pumps, though certified installer shortages remain a bottleneck.

green.headline: Zero Carbon by 2040, Nationalise Energy & Stop All Fossil Fuels
green.summary: Bring target date for Net Zero forward to 2040, bring Big 5 energy retail companies into public ownership, cancel all new fossil fuel projects, and ban domestic flights where train alternatives exist.
keyPoints: Zero carbon emissions target by 2040 (a decade ahead of current UK law)
Nationalise the National Grid, water companies, and energy supply companies
Invest £40bn per year in wind, tidal, solar, and national grid energy storage
Comprehensive ban on all oil and gas exploration, extraction, and airport expansions
green.factCheckSnippet: IFS: Full nationalisation of utilities requires substantial compensation outlays or major bond issuances under international investment treaties.

snp.headline: Scotland as European Green Powerhouse & Just Transition
snp.summary: Capitalise on Scotland's 25% of Europe's offshore wind potential, fund a Just Transition for North Sea oil and gas workers, and demand full devolution of energy powers.
keyPoints: Ensure Scottish communities directly share revenue from the ScotWind leasing rounds
Oppose reckless cliff-edge cessation of oil licenses while prioritizing worker retraining
Reform the national grid transmission charging system that penalises Scottish renewable producers
Demands £500m Just Transition Fund for North East Scotland
snp.costEstimate: Funded through Scottish energy revenues and ScotWind returns
snp.factCheckSnippet: Ofgem / National Grid: Scottish energy generators currently pay higher transmission grid charges due to distance from southern population centres.
snp.factCheckSource: House of Commons Scottish Affairs Committee

plaid.headline: Welsh Renewable Wealth Retention & Crown Estate Devolution
plaid.summary: Devolve the Crown Estate to Wales (as in Scotland) so that offshore wind revenues stay in Wales; create a 100% renewable Wales by 2035.
keyPoints: Devolve management of Crown Estate seabed and mineral rights to Wales (£1bn+ value)
Ynni Cymru: Welsh publicly owned renewable energy developer
Target 100% of Welsh electricity demand from renewables by 2035
Ban all new opencast coal mining and oil drilling permits in Wales
plaid.costEstimate: Financed by retaining Welsh Crown Estate profits in the Senedd
plaid.factCheckSnippet: Welsh Government / Crown Estate data: Crown Estate in Scotland was successfully devolved under the Scotland Act 2016, generating direct revenue for Holyrood.

restore.headline: Energy Independence, Coal & Gas Revival, End Green Taxes
restore.summary: Dismantle green subsidies, reopen British coal and gas reserves, achieve cheap and resilient base-load power, and withdraw from the Paris Climate Accord.
keyPoints: Withdraw the United Kingdom from the Paris Climate Accord and COP treaties
Immediately decommission inefficient wind turbines relying on taxpayer subsidies
Drill for domestic oil and gas with zero green surcharge to deliver cheap industrial energy
Re-commission domestic coal-fired generation stations for continuous industrial manufacturing
restore.costEstimate: Self-funding through elimination of £10bn+ annual green support schemes
restore.factCheckSnippet: International Energy Agency (IEA): New solar and wind generation are now cheaper per megawatt-hour than building new coal or gas peaking plants.

compass.summary: Green transition, public energy, climate regulations

title: Housing Targets, Planning Reform & Renters' Rights
description: Housebuilding targets, mandatory council quotas, brownfield vs greenbelt, and renters' rights legislation.

officialFigureBenchmark.label: Annual Net Additional UK Dwellings
officialFigureBenchmark.source: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government (MHCLG)

publicOpinionQuestion: Should the government build on 'grey belt' land to solve the national housing crisis?

labour.headline: 1.5 Million Homes Target & Release the 'Grey Belt'
labour.summary: Mandatory local housing targets restored; build 1.5 million homes over the parliament; release low-quality 'grey belt' greenbelt land; pass the Renters' Rights Bill abolishing Section 21 evictions.
keyPoints: Build 1.5 million homes over the parliament with mandatory local targets
Prioritise brownfield and poor-quality 'grey belt' (e.g. neglected car parks on greenbelt)
Renters' Rights Bill: ban 'no-fault' Section 21 evictions and end bidding wars
Deliver the biggest boost to social and affordable housing in a generation
labour.costEstimate: Private-sector driven via planning deregulation plus targeted social housing capital
labour.factCheckSnippet: Planning Advisory Service: Reaching 300,000 homes a year requires massive expansion in bricklayers, electricians, and local planning officers.

conservative.headline: 1.6 Million Homes on Brownfield & Protect the Green Belt
conservative.summary: Build 1.6 million homes strictly on urban brownfield land while defending greenbelt open spaces; expand Help to Buy; abolish stamp duty for first-time buyers up to £425,000.
keyPoints: Permanent stamp duty exemption for first-time buyers on homes up to £425,000
Introduce a new Help to Buy equity loan scheme for first-time purchasers
Protect the greenbelt from aggressive development by focusing density in city centres
Abolish EU legacy 'nutrient neutrality' laws to unlock 100,000 stalled builds
conservative.costEstimate: Help to Buy equity loans cost approx. £1bn - £2bn in revolving capital
conservative.factCheckSnippet: House of Commons Housing Committee: Brownfield sites alone in high-demand regions (London/South East) are insufficient to reach 1.6M homes.

reform.headline: 'British Homes for British Workers': Citizen-Only Social Housing & Fast-Track Brownfield
reform.summary: Mandate that social and council housing is reserved strictly for British citizens, immediately end Home Office procurement of private rental properties for asylum seekers, cut net migration to relieve housing demand, and fast-track brownfield regeneration while repealing landlord regulations that shrink rental supply.
keyPoints: Strict British Citizen Priority for Social Housing: legally require British citizenship and local multi-year residency for all council and housing association allocations ('British Homes for British Workers')
Ban Asylum Seeker Use of Private Rental Stock: prohibit the Home Office and Serco/Mears contractors from outbidding local renters for private houses and HMOs
Relieve Demand via Net-Zero Essential Migration: curb population-driven housing pressure by freezing non-essential immigration and student dependants

Fast-Track Brownfield & Protect Private Landlords: grant automatic 4-week planning approvals on urban brownfield sites, scrap nutrient neutrality and Section 106 delays for SME builders, and repeal punitive landlord rules
reform.costEstimate: Market-led brownfield incentives; saves £2bn+/yr ending private asylum accommodation contracts
reform.targetTimeline: Immediate statutory housing allocation directive in Year 1
reform.factCheckSnippet: Chartered Institute of Housing: Around 90% of social housing lets already go to UK nationals, though ending private asylum dispersal contracts would free up localized HMO stock.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK Housing, Planning & Social Allocation Platform

libdem.headline: 380,000 Homes a Year & 150,000 for Social Rent
libdem.summary: Build 380,000 new homes annually including 150,000 social homes, give local communities 'first refusal' on developments, and introduce 'use-it-or-lose-it' rules for developers.
keyPoints: Mandate 150,000 new social rent homes every year built to high environmental standards
Abolish 'no-fault' evictions and give tenants 3-year standard tenancies
Empower councils to enforce 'use-it-or-lose-it' land taxes on developers hoarding land
Require all new homes to feature solar panels and zero-carbon heat pumps
libdem.costEstimate: £6bn annual capital borrowing programme for social housing
libdem.factCheckSnippet: Shelter / Crisis: 150,000 social homes per year matches independent estimates needed to eradicate homelessness.

green.headline: 150,000 Council Homes, Rent Caps & End Right to Buy
green.summary: Build 150,000 council homes a year, empower local authorities to implement local rent controls, end the Right to Buy scheme, and retrofit all existing homes with insulation.
keyPoints: Build 150,000 high-spec social rented council homes per year
End the 'Right to Buy' scheme to permanently safeguard council housing stock
Empower local councils to introduce rent control caps linked to local average wages
Massive national retrofit scheme to bring all UK homes to Energy Performance Band B
green.costEstimate: £12bn annual social housing grant funded by wealth tax
green.factCheckSnippet: Institute of Economic Affairs / Centre for Cities: Strict rent controls in Berlin and Scotland historically reduced overall rental supply on the market.

snp.headline: Deliver 110,000 Affordable Homes & Scottish Rent Caps
snp.summary: Target 110,000 affordable homes in Scotland by 2032 with 70% for social rent, maintain strong Scottish tenant protections, and reverse UK housing benefit cuts.
keyPoints: Invest £3.5bn towards delivering 110,000 Scottish affordable homes by 2032
Maintain Scotland's pioneering permanent rent control frameworks for designated hotspots
Demand UK restoration of Local Housing Allowance rates to track real market rents
Full devolution of borrowing limits for Scottish municipal councils
snp.factCheckSnippet: Scottish Parliament Information Centre (SPICe): Scottish budget reductions in 2024 forced temporary slowing of the 110k target timeline.

plaid.headline: Protect Welsh Rural Communities & Second Home Restrictions
plaid.summary: Overhaul Welsh housing supply, empower councils to levy 300% council tax on empty second homes, build high-spec social housing, and prevent rural depopulation.
keyPoints: Grant councils power to charge up to 300% council tax premiums on holiday and second homes
Introduce local community approval for converting family homes into holiday lets
Deliver 10,000 council and social homes across Wales over 5 years
End 'no fault' evictions and install rent control mechanisms in high-cost Welsh areas
plaid.costEstimate: Funded through second home council tax premiums
plaid.factCheckSnippet: Welsh Local Government Association: Second-home premiums in Gwynedd and Pembrokeshire raised tens of millions for local affordable home schemes.

restore.headline: Abolish Planning Permission for Brownfield & Traditional Architecture
restore.summary: Abolish the Town and Country Planning Act 1947, permit automatic right-to-build on brownfield land, mandate traditional British aesthetic design codes, and ban foreign corporate ownership of housing.
keyPoints: Repeal restrictive planning laws and replace with simple property rights
Ban overseas non-resident individuals and international venture funds from buying British homes
Enforce traditional vernacular architectural design codes for all new developments
Full tax write-offs for building materials manufactured inside the UK
restore.factCheckSnippet: Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA): Deregulating design and planning creates risk of substandard construction without proper building control oversight.

compass.summary: Planning deregulation vs council housing & tenant rights

title: State Pension Triple Lock & Adult Social Care
description: Long-term indexation of the UK state pension, personal allowance tax thresholds for retirees, and funding adult social care.
publicOpinionQuestion: Should the State Pension Triple Lock be protected indefinitely?

labour.headline: Maintain Triple Lock This Parliament; 2030 Double Lock Transition to Fund National Care
labour.summary: Guarantee the triple lock through this Parliament; transition from 2030 to a double lock (earnings or inflation), redirecting £4bn/yr long-term savings into establishing the new National Care Service, while ensuring state pension does not get dragged into income tax.
keyPoints: Legally protect the triple lock through 2029
Transition to double lock (earnings or inflation) from April 2030
Ring-fence £4bn/year long-term savings directly to fund the National Care Service
Ensure low-income pensioners relying solely on the state pension do not pay income tax
labour.costEstimate: Neutral in short-term; saves ~£4bn/yr from 2030 to fund care
labour.factCheckSnippet: IFS: The transition provides a fiscally sustainable path to fund adult social care without general taxation spikes.

conservative.headline: Defend Triple Lock Plus: Raise Pensioner Tax Allowance in Lockstep
conservative.summary: Unconditionally protect the state pension triple lock and introduce 'Triple Lock Plus', raising the tax-free personal allowance for pensioners each year so the state pension is never taxed.
keyPoints: Oppose any dilution or watering down of the triple lock
Legislate Triple Lock Plus to ensure the state pension never incurs income tax
Oppose Burnham's 2030 double lock care transition
Cut Whitehall quango budgets to support adult social care locally
conservative.costEstimate: Estimated £2.4bn - £3.1bn per year for Triple Lock Plus tax relief
conservative.factCheckSnippet: Full Fact: State pension on track to overtake personal allowance (£12,570) by 2027 without policy adjustment.

reform.headline: Ban Foreign Nationals from Welfare, 20-Hr Work Mandate, Restore Winter Fuel & Triple Lock
reform.summary: Overhaul the UK welfare state to save tens of billions by barring all non-UK citizens (including settled status holders) from Universal Credit and welfare benefits, requiring fit-to-work claimants to do 20 hours/week of community work, overhauling PIP assessments, restoring universal Winter Fuel Payments, and protecting the State Pension Triple Lock.
keyPoints: Total Welfare Ban for Foreign Nationals: restrict Universal Credit, child benefit, and non-contributory welfare strictly to British citizens, removing entitlement from settled foreign nationals and visa holders

Mandatory 20-Hour/Week Community Work & 2-Strike Job Rule: require long-term unemployed claimants deemed fit to work to complete 20 hours/week of civic community work and withdraw benefits if two job offers are refused
PIP & Disability Benefit Overhaul: enforce in-person medical assessments and replace cash PIP payments for mild anxiety/depression claims with targeted treatment and in-kind support

Protect Triple Lock, Restore Winter Fuel & Working-Family Child Cap: unconditionally protect the State Pension Triple Lock, restore universal Winter Fuel Payments, and enforce the two-child benefit cap with exemptions strictly for full-time working British couples
reform.costEstimate: Claims £15bn–£25bn/yr savings from foreign national welfare ban and PIP/workfare reforms
reform.targetTimeline: Immediate Year 1 Welfare Reform & Citizens Entitlement Bill
reform.factCheckSnippet: IFS / OBR: Barring non-citizens from Universal Credit yields multi-billion savings but requires overturning EU Withdrawal Agreement settled-status treaty rights.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK Welfare Overhaul, Winter Fuel & Pensioner Guarantee

libdem.headline: Legally Enshrine Triple Lock & £5bn Free Personal Adult Social Care
libdem.summary: Legislate to guarantee the state pension triple lock every year of Parliament, paired with an immediate £5bn national package for free personal adult social care.
keyPoints: Legally enshrine the triple lock in primary legislation
£5bn free personal adult social care for older and disabled people
Introduce Carer's Minimum Wage 20% above National Living Wage
Fund via windfall taxes on energy super-profits and big tech levies
libdem.factCheckSnippet: King's Fund: Free personal care would dramatically alleviate hospital discharge gridlock.
libdem.factCheckSource: The King's Fund / Lib Dem Costing

green.headline: Protect Triple Lock, Increase Base State Pension & Trial UBI
green.summary: Maintain the triple lock, benchmark the base state pension upward to provide genuine retirement dignity, and pilot a Universal Basic Income.
keyPoints: Maintain the triple lock and increase base state pension
Universal free personal social care funded by progressive taxation
Introduce 1-2% wealth tax on fortunes over £10m to fund care and pensions
Nationalise water and public utilities to lower pensioner utility bills
green.costEstimate: Funded via £15bn annual wealth tax on multi-millionaires
green.factCheckSnippet: Full Fact: Wealth tax revenue estimates vary widely based on behavioural capital flight.

snp.headline: Defend Triple Lock Unconditionally & Fast-Track WASPI Compensation
snp.summary: Demand total UK Government protection for the triple lock, reject any double lock dilution, and immediately deliver compensation for 1950s-born WASPI women.
keyPoints: Uncompromising defence of the state pension triple lock
Immediate statutory financial compensation for WASPI women affected by pension age changes
Devolve full employment, pension, and welfare powers to Holyrood
Scrap the punitive two-child benefit cap immediately
snp.factCheckSnippet: Parliamentary Ombudsman (PHSO): Recommended compensation between £1,000 and £2,950 per affected woman.

plaid.headline: Protect Triple Lock, End Rural Fuel Poverty & Deliver WASPI Justice
plaid.summary: Protect the triple lock, implement PHSO recommendations for WASPI women, and introduce a Welsh rural energy social tariff for older households.
keyPoints: Retain the triple lock without exceptions
Full compensation for 1950s women under PHSO findings
Social energy tariff for off-gas grid Welsh rural pensioners
Replace Barnett formula to secure £1.2bn additional annual funding for Welsh health and care
plaid.costEstimate: Part of £1.2bn/year needs-based funding formula reform
plaid.factCheckSnippet: Welsh Governance Centre: Replacing Barnett with a needs-based formula yields approx £1.2bn extra per year for Wales.

restore.headline: Shield Pensioners from Stealth Taxes & Repeal Green Levies
restore.summary: Retain the state pension triple lock, abolish green levies and Net Zero charges on elderly household bills, and index tax allowances to protect pensioners.
keyPoints: Retain state pension purchasing power
Abolish all green levies on domestic gas and electricity to reduce heating bills by £300/yr
Repeal stealth tax freezing of personal allowances
Reclaim foreign aid funds to support domestic elder care
restore.costEstimate: Estimated £8bn/yr saved from Net Zero subsidies
restore.factCheckSnippet: Ofgem: Green levies currently account for approx £100-£170 of average annual domestic energy bills.

compass.summary: State pension protection & nationalised care service

title: Education, School Funding & University Tuition
description: State school funding, VAT on independent school fees, early-years childcare, curriculum reform, university tuition fees, and student loan interest.

compass.summary: State school funding, tuition fees, private school taxation

officialFigureBenchmark.label: Current UK Schools & Higher Education Budget
officialFigureBenchmark.value: approx. £61.6bn core state schools budget; university tuition fees capped at £9,250 - £9,535/yr
officialFigureBenchmark.source: Department for Education (DfE) / Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS)

publicOpinionQuestion: Do you support applying standard 20% VAT to private school fees to fund state education?

labour.headline: Apply 20% VAT on Private School Fees to Fund 6,500 State Teachers
labour.summary: Ending the tax break on private school fees by applying standard 20% VAT and removing business rates relief, ring-fencing ~£1.5bn annually to hire 6,500 new expert state school teachers, establish mental health support in every school, and expand free breakfast clubs in all primary schools.
keyPoints: Standard 20% VAT applied to private school fees from January 2025 onwards
Recruit 6,500 new specialized state school teachers in STEM and shortage subjects
Free breakfast clubs for every primary school student across England
Launch Skills England to reform the Apprenticeship Levy and boost technical qualifications
Ongoing review into long-term higher education funding and student maintenance
labour.costEstimate: Yields estimated £1.3bn - £1.7bn annual revenue for state schools
labour.factCheckSnippet: IFS analysis confirms VAT on private school fees raises ~£1.3bn-£1.5bn net, though private pupil transfers to state sector could absorb ~£100m-£300m.
labour.factCheckSource: Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) Education Briefing
labour.officialSourceTitle: Labour Manifesto: Break Down Barriers to Opportunity

conservative.headline: Protect Independent Schools from VAT & Introduce Mandatory National Service at 18
conservative.summary: Opposing punitive VAT on independent schools which burdens state capacity; rolling out the Advanced British Standard combining A-levels and T-levels; legislating mandatory National Service for all 18-year-olds (military academy or civic community service); and defending free speech on university campuses.
keyPoints: Oppose and repeal VAT on independent school tuition fees
Deliver the Advanced British Standard replacing A-levels with broader post-16 qualifications
Introduce mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (30,000 military places + civic volunteering)
Strict statutory guidance on gender identity in schools and safeguarding single-sex spaces
Enforce Higher Education (Freedom of Speech) Act to fine universities canceling speakers
conservative.costEstimate: National Service estimated at £2.5bn/yr; ABS transition funded through DfE baseline
conservative.factCheckSnippet: Full Fact notes: The £2.5bn National Service plan would be partially funded by repurposing the UK Shared Prosperity Fund.
conservative.factCheckSource: Full Fact / House of Commons Library

reform.headline: Repeal Private School VAT, 20% Fee Tax Relief, Scrap Loan Interest & Ban Gender Ideology
reform.summary: Led by Shadow Education Spokesperson Suella Braverman: immediately repeal Labour’s 20% VAT on independent schools and grant 20% tax relief on private school fees, scrap student loan interest, defund low-value university courses in favour of trade apprenticeships, and enforce a statutory ban on gender ideology and critical race theory in schools.
keyPoints: Repeal 20% VAT & Grant 20% Tax Relief on Independent Schools: reverse Labour’s private school VAT policy and provide a 20% tax deduction for parents paying independent school fees to relieve state classroom overcrowding

Scrap Student Loan Interest & Mandate 2-Year Degrees: abolish interest on student loans (0% real rate), require universities to offer fast-track 2-year degrees, and cut funding for low-employability courses

Statutory Ban on Gender Ideology & Critical Race Theory: prohibit schools from teaching contested gender identity concepts or critical race theory, mandating parental notification and single-sex spaces

Patriotic Curriculum & Technical Apprenticeships: require balanced teaching of British imperial and constitutional history and redirect university subsidies into vocational engineering, construction, and trade apprenticeships
reform.costEstimate: Estimated £4bn–£5bn/yr for student loan interest abolition and £1.5bn/yr for independent school tax relief
reform.factCheckSnippet: IFS Education Analysis: Repealing VAT on private schools and adding 20% tax relief costs ~£3bn/yr net, primarily benefiting higher-income households.
reform.officialSourceTitle: Reform UK Education, Universities & Parental Rights Platform

libdem.headline: Free School Meals for All Primary Children & Rejoin EU Erasmus+ Student Programme
libdem.summary: Expand free school meals to all 4.6 million primary school pupils; boost the Pupil Premium by £390 per disadvantaged pupil; station a qualified mental health practitioner in every school; and rejoin the EU's Erasmus+ university exchange programme.
keyPoints: Universal free school meals for all primary school pupils, extended to all children in poverty in secondary schools
Increase the Pupil Premium by £390 per year to close the post-pandemic attainment gap
Rejoin the European Union Erasmus+ student exchange programme
A mental health specialist in every primary and secondary school
Exempt children with special educational needs (EHCPs) from any private school fee tax measures
libdem.costEstimate: Free school meals expansion estimated at ~£1.1bn/yr; funded via Digital Services Tax surcharge
libdem.factCheckSnippet: Full Fact: Expanding free school meals to all primary pupils costs £1bn annually; Lib Dem tax targets on tech giants match this scale.
libdem.officialSourceTitle: Liberal Democrat Manifesto: Fair Deal for Education

green.headline: Abolish University Tuition Fees Entirely, Scrap Ofsted & £3bn Green Schools Fund
green.summary: Abolish university tuition fees and reinstate maintenance grants; abolish high-stakes testing, SATs, and Ofsted inspections, replacing them with supportive local moderation; end academisation and return all schools to local authorities; and provide £3bn in capital funding to make all school buildings energy-efficient.
keyPoints: Abolish all higher education tuition fees for undergraduate degrees across the UK
Scrap Ofsted and replace with collaborative local authority peer assessments
End the academies programme and return state schools to democratic local council oversight
Universal free school meals for all primary and secondary school pupils
£3bn capital investment to retrofit schools with solar panels, heat pumps, and modern ventilation
green.costEstimate: Abolishing tuition fees and restoring grants estimated at £9bn - £11bn/yr; funded via Wealth Tax
green.targetTimeline: Roll-out within first two budget cycles
green.factCheckSnippet: IFS calculates: Abolishing tuition fees costs ~£10bn annually in public borrowing or requires equivalent wealth taxation revenue.
green.officialSourceTitle: Green Party Manifesto: Real Hope, Real Change for Education

snp.headline: Maintain Free University Tuition in Scotland & Protect Scottish Childcare Devolution
snp.summary: Uncompromising commitment to free university tuition for Scottish undergraduates studying in Scotland, saving Scottish students up to £27,750; ongoing delivery of 1,140 hours of funded early learning and childcare; and targeted Scottish Attainment Challenge funding.
keyPoints: Maintain free university tuition for all eligible Scottish students studying in Scotland
Expand funded early learning and childcare to 1- and 2-year-olds from low-income families
Invest £1bn over parliament in the Scottish Attainment Challenge to close the poverty-related attainment gap
Demand compensation and UK-wide funding parity following changes to English student finance
snp.costEstimate: Free Scottish tuition costs Scottish Government approximately £900m/yr
snp.factCheckSnippet: Audit Scotland: Free tuition saves Scottish graduates significant debt, though university sector warns of funding pressures on domestic student caps.
snp.factCheckSource: Audit Scotland / Scottish Parliament Information Centre (SPICe)
snp.officialSourceTitle: SNP Policy Platform: Defending Scotland's Education

plaid.headline: Fully Devolve Education & Student Loans to Wales, Expand Welsh-Medium Schools
plaid.summary: Full devolution of all remaining education and student finance powers to the Senedd; universal free school meals for all primary pupils across Wales; aggressive expansion of Welsh-medium nursery and secondary education; and higher living-cost maintenance grants for Welsh students.
keyPoints: Devolve student loan administration and repayment rules to the Senedd
Universal free school meals delivered to every primary child in Wales
Target 1 million Welsh speakers by 2050 via Welsh-medium education expansion
Increase maintenance grants for Welsh students to match the real living wage
plaid.costEstimate: Devolved Welsh education block grant adjustment + £150m targeted Welsh-medium investment
plaid.factCheckSnippet: Senedd Research confirms: Wales is already delivering universal primary free school meals, leading UK nations in early-years nutritional rollout.
plaid.factCheckSource: Senedd Research / Welsh Government Education Data
plaid.officialSourceTitle: Plaid Cymru Policy: An Education System for Wales

restore.headline: Restore Classical STEM Curriculum, Defund Ideological Courses & Expand Grammar Schools
restore.summary: Focus state education strictly on rigorous STEM, core literacy, and British constitutional history; eliminate politicised training and DEI modules; remove barriers to creating new grammar schools; and replace degree expansion with traditional manufacturing apprenticeships.
keyPoints: Rigorous return to classical academic standards: STEM, mathematics, grammar, and sovereign history
Repeal the ban on establishing new state-funded grammar schools
Defund university degrees that fail to generate net positive tax contributions within 5 years
Direct £2bn in university subsidies toward technical polytechnics and industrial trades
restore.costEstimate: Net neutral via reallocation of university teaching subsidies to trade polytechnics
restore.factCheckSnippet: Education Policy Institute: Expanding grammar schools historically correlates with increased social segregation, though supporters cite high academic attainment.
